title: Build education machines: AI + education should create human capital, not study tools
summary: Farza argues the biggest AI + education opportunity is end-to-end "machines" that take someone from a 2/10 to a 6/10 in their ability to pursue a goal, not tools that help students study. Pure learning is hard to monetize, while outcomes are what people pay for. AI could finally scale the accountability, structure and motivation that only high-touch human programs delivered.

principles.text: People learn in order to do something, so build for the outcome rather than the act of learning.
principles.quote: Very few people learn to just learn. They learn so they can _do_ something.

principles.text: Pure learning products cap out on monetization; people won't pay much or for long without a clear result in sight.
principles.quote: **And, you can only monetize straight up “learning” so much.**

principles.text: Reframe education companies as machines that build human capital, and judge them by how far they move a person on a 1-10 capability scale.
principles.quote: Machines where a person who is a 2/10 in their ability to impact the world + pursue their goals in some domain walks in, and can walk out at least a 6/10.

principles.text: Content doesn't transform people; the right mix of learning, accountability, structure and motivation does.
principles.quote: It’s offering the right balance of learning, accountability, and structure. All while properly maintaining your motivation.

principles.text: The best outcome machines are high-touch and human-led, so they don't scale. AI is the first chance to extend that access.
principles.quote: But for the first time ever, AI can change that.

principles.text: Build goal-specific end-to-end machines (YouTuber, author, coder, salesperson, filmmaker) instead of generic study tools.
principles.quote: It’s in building better end-to-end machines that output human capital.
